name: Cross-Rate via Direct Multiplication
meaning: Derives a cross-rate between currencies A and C from two quotes sharing common currency B, when B cancels directly (denominator of one quote, numerator of the other).

variables.C/A: the derived cross-rate, units of C per unit of A
variables.C/B: a known quote, units of C per unit of B
variables.B/A: a known quote, units of B per unit of A

intuition: The shared currency B cancels algebraically exactly like a common factor, leaving the direct C/A relationship.
commonMistake: Multiplying two quotes where the shared currency occupies the same position in both, which does not cancel and produces a meaningless result.

name: Cross-Rate via Inversion
meaning: Derives a cross-rate when the shared currency occupies the same position (both numerators, or both denominators) in the two given quotes, requiring one quote to be inverted before multiplying.

variables.B/A: a known quote sharing currency A with the second quote in the same position
variables.C/A: a known quote sharing currency A with the first quote in the same position

intuition: Inverting one quote moves the shared currency to the opposite position, allowing it to cancel exactly as in direct multiplication.
commonMistake: Forgetting to relabel which currency is the price currency and which is the base currency after inverting.

name: Forward Rate from Points
meaning: Converts quoted forward points into an outright forward rate by adding the scaled points to the spot rate.

variables.points: the quoted forward points, scaled to the last decimal place of the spot quote (÷100 instead of ÷10,000 for JPY pairs)

intuition: Forward points are simply the forward-minus-spot difference pre-scaled for convenient quotation; dividing back by the scaling factor recovers the actual rate difference.
commonMistake: Using the ÷10,000 scaling factor on a JPY pair instead of ÷100, producing a forward rate barely different from spot.
relatedLearningOutcome: explain the arbitrage relationship between spot and forward exchange rates and interest rates, calculate a forward rate using points or in percentage terms, and interpret a forward discount or premium

name: Forward Premium/Discount, Percentage Terms
meaning: Expresses the forward premium or discount as a percentage of the spot rate rather than in points; the reverse relationship S × (1 + % premium/discount) = F recovers the forward rate from a percentage.
intuition: A positive result means the base currency is at a forward premium; a negative result means it is at a forward discount.
commonMistake: Reversing a percentage premium/discount back to the spot rate by subtracting instead of dividing.
relatedLearningOutcome: explain the arbitrage relationship between spot and forward exchange rates and interest rates, calculate a forward rate using points or in percentage terms, and interpret a forward discount or premium

name: Core Arbitrage (No-Arbitrage) Relationship
meaning: The no-arbitrage condition linking the spot rate, the forward rate, and the domestic and foreign interest rates, such that borrowing domestically, converting spot, investing abroad, and hedging back forward yields exactly the domestic risk-free return.

variables.r_d: the domestic (base-currency-side) interest rate, over the same period as the forward
variables.r_f: the foreign (price-currency-side) interest rate, same period
variables.S(f/d): the spot rate, foreign (price) currency per unit of domestic (base) currency
variables.F(f/d): the forward rate, same f/d quoting convention as the spot rate

intuition: If the quoted forward rate does not satisfy this equation, a riskless arbitrage profit is available by borrowing at the relatively cheap rate and investing at the relatively rich rate, hedged forward.
workedExample: S(f/d)=1.4200, r_d=2.50%, r_f=4.00%: solving for F gives F=1.4408 (see the forward-rate-solved formula for the rearranged version).
commonMistake: Mixing f/d and d/f quoted data within the same calculation instead of converting everything to one consistent convention first.
relatedLearningOutcome: explain the arbitrage relationship between spot and forward exchange rates and interest rates, calculate a forward rate using points or in percentage terms, and interpret a forward discount or premium

name: Forward Rate Solved from the Arbitrage Relationship
meaning: The core arbitrage relationship rearranged to solve directly for the no-arbitrage forward rate given the spot rate and both interest rates.

variables.S(f/d): the spot rate, foreign (price) currency per unit of domestic (base) currency

intuition: The currency with the lower interest rate always trades at a forward premium; the currency with the higher interest rate always trades at a forward discount, regardless of quoting convention.
commonMistake: Swapping which rate belongs in the numerator (foreign) versus the denominator (domestic), which inverts the direction of the computed premium/discount.
relatedLearningOutcome: explain the arbitrage relationship between spot and forward exchange rates and interest rates, calculate a forward rate using points or in percentage terms, and interpret a forward discount or premium

name: Forward Rate as Expected Future Spot Rate
meaning: If the forward rate is treated as an unbiased predictor of the future spot rate, this gives the implied expected percentage appreciation or depreciation of the base currency.

variables.F_t: the forward rate quoted today for settlement at t+1
variables.S_t+1: the future spot rate at t+1, assumed equal to F_t under this interpretation

intuition: This equation reframes the arbitrage relationship as an expectation rather than a hedged, riskless position; the source is explicit that forward rates may be unbiased but are historically poor predictors of the actual future spot rate.
workedExample: r_d=2.50%, r_f=4.00%: implied expected appreciation of the base currency ≈ (0.0400−0.0250)/1.0250 = 1.46%.
commonMistake: Treating 'unbiased predictor' as meaning 'accurate predictor' — an unbiased forecast can still have a very large margin of error on any single occasion.
relatedLearningOutcome: explain the arbitrage relationship between spot and forward exchange rates and interest rates, calculate a forward rate using points or in percentage terms, and interpret a forward discount or premium

name: Day-Count-Adjusted Forward Points and Forward Rate
meaning: Generalizes the arbitrage relationship to periods other than a full year, using τ (the fraction of a year, typically days/360 on a Libor actual/360 basis) to scale the annualized interest rates to the forward's actual maturity.

variables.τ: the fraction of a year the forward covers, typically days ÷ 360

intuition: Because the (1 + r_d·τ) denominator term grows with τ, forward points do not scale in exact linear proportion to the time horizon, even though they scale approximately in proportion to it.
commonMistake: Omitting the (1 + r_d·τ) denominator term, which gives a close but not exact answer, or assuming points exactly double when the horizon doubles.
relatedLearningOutcome: explain the arbitrage relationship between spot and forward exchange rates and interest rates, calculate a forward rate using points or in percentage terms, and interpret a forward discount or premium
